question: R-C9-80: a library clip for a TWO-HANDED Meteor -- both hands on the shaft, a stamp that reads as a PLANT at the three-quarter-front camera, a clean release
screen: 678 library motions searched by name/category; 12 previews viewed free (the CDN preview GIFs, 8-14 frames each): 4, 86, 102, 125, 126, 128, 149, 237, 240, 241, 242, 382. Only 4 'Attack' and 128 'Heavy Hammer Swing' put both hands together on a raised handle; both fetched on HER rig (6 of 9 credits).

004 Attack (2.80 s).hands: TOGETHER: 0.136 m apart median -- a two-handed grip

upright_blend.why: she hunches with her head straight over her low hands: a vertical staff through the fist runs up through her head

release.note: clean (one peak) but a one-frame snap: the hands drop 0.68 m between two 30 fps keys

128 Heavy Hammer Swing (1.83 s).hands: APART: 0.536 m median -- a long-handle grip; the swing is a diagonal to his lower left, not a stamp

verdict: NOTHING USABLE IN THE LIBRARY. 004 is two-handed but its slam cannot be a plant: upright, the staff runs through her head (109 of 200 verts inside); leaned 30 deg forward it clears the head but grazes the thigh (28) and reads as a diagonal at the three-quarter camera -- the pass-2 Meteor's own problem; seated, the crown points DOWN at the slam and 383 verts are in her legs. 128 is not two-handed on one short grip at all (hands 0.54 m apart, off hand never within 0.30 m of the shaft) and penetrates on every treatment (737). The remaining 3 credits were NOT spent: no other previewed clip brings both hands together over a vertical shaft.
